author: Nick Fenley
title: Fresno-area junior college district investigating video of Lake Tahoe beach brawl - NewsBreak
text:
By Nick Fenley ,
10 hours ago SCCCD administrative offices are located at 1171 Fulton Street in downtown Fresno, California. Photographed Wednesday, June 10, 2026. ERIC PAUL ZAMORA/ezamora@fresnobee.com The State Center Community College District is investigating a viral video that shows two men — reportedly both athletics employees of the district — involved in a physical alternation on a Lake Tahoe beach.
According to an Instagram video uploaded May 31, the altercation unfolded at Zephyr Cove, on the Nevada side of the popular tourist destination. The video appears to show Madera Community College athletics director Jesse White and Fresno City College athletics director Derrick Johnson.
In the posted video of the altercation, one of the men is sitting on top of another man, Johnson, who is prone on the beach. White straddles Johnson and can be heard cursing at him while holding him down.
A couple of bystanders attempt to get White off of Johnson. At one point, White tosses Johnson’s sunglasses off his face and asks what he’s going to do.
White eventually gets off of Johnson and picks up a nearby backpack-style cooler. Johnson tells White to give him the cooler, and White responds by punching Johnson.
The pair resume scuffling on the ground before White picks up the cooler again and the video ends.
As of Wednesday, the Instagram video has gotten more than 17,000 likes and been shared more than 10,000 times.
SCCCD spokesperson Jill Wagner confirmed the district’s investigation of the video but did not provide any additional details.
White and Johnson didn’t respond to The Bee’s requests for comment.
Messages sent to the Instagram user who uploaded the video, as well as another man who identified himself as being in the video, went unread.
People chimed in to share their thoughts in the comment section of the video.
“Disappointing with these educators. They are expected to be leaders and represent their college and be role models for their student athletes. The question is, how will their administration handle this,” one person wrote on Wednesday.
The Douglas County Sheriff’s Office wasn’t able to confirm whether deputies responded to any reports of a disturbance at the scene on May 31.
The annual California Community College Athletic Directors Association convention was held in South Lake Tahoe June 1–4.
SCCCD is based in Fresno and oversees Fresno City College and Madera Community College, along with Reedley College, Clovis Community College and Madera Community College at Oakhurst.
